passage:
Notes on Eshaan, Wednesday. He came to my desk furious: the accounts team had been told to backdate leave records so that contract staff would lose paid leave they had earned. He wanted to email the whole company that night. I asked him to wait. Over the week he copied the leave sheets, found two colleagues who had seen the same instruction, and filed a written complaint with the HR grievance committee. He knows his manager may freeze his promotion. He is calmer now, not calm. He said, "I'd rather lose the promotion than sign it." I will go with him to the hearing.

Mridul

qa.q: What had the accounts team been told to do with the leave records?
qa.a: They had been told to backdate the leave records so contract staff would lose paid leave they had earned.

qa.q: What does Eshaan's remark about the promotion suggest about what he cares about?
qa.a: It suggests he values acting honestly over advancing, and that his anger has turned into a firm decision, even though he knows it may cost him.

qa.q: Why was gathering the sheets and finding colleagues a stronger move than emailing the whole company?
qa.a: It gave him evidence and allies and sent the concern through a proper channel, which protects him and makes it harder to dismiss.

qa.q: How might the contract staff see Eshaan's complaint?
qa.a: They may feel relief and hope that someone is standing up for them, and perhaps some worry about what happens to Eshaan.

grounding: Shows an employee channelling moral outrage at workplace injustice into evidence, allies and a formal complaint, accepting personal cost.

passage:
Tuesday night.

I'm still shaking. Today I saw the safety officer at the Thane site sign off twenty harness inspections without touching a single harness. Twenty. Men climb on those every day.

My first thought was to shout at him in front of everyone. My second was to post the photos online. I did neither.

Instead I took dated photos of the harnesses and the signed forms. At lunch I told Lalit, who works the night shift. He said, "Mohit, I've seen the same thing. I'll sign with you." Then we found the company's safety complaint address and wrote a plain, factual report with the photos.

Lalit warned me they might move me off the project. He might be right. I'm scared about that.

But I'd rather be moved than read about a fall I could have stopped. Sent the report at 9:14 p.m. Now I'm going to try and sleep.

qa.q: How many harness inspections did the safety officer sign off without checking?
qa.a: The safety officer signed off twenty harness inspections.

qa.q: What was Mohit feeling about the report and the risk of being moved?
qa.a: Mohit felt outraged and shaken by the unsafe sign-offs, and scared about being moved off the project, yet determined.

qa.q: How did Mohit channel the anger usefully?
qa.a: Mohit gathered dated evidence, found an ally in Lalit and used the company's proper complaint channel instead of shouting or posting online.

qa.q: How might the workers who climb on those harnesses see Mohit's report if they knew?
qa.a: The workers would probably feel protected and grateful, since the report could prevent a fall.

grounding: Shows a young worker channelling moral outrage at an unsafe institution into evidence, allies and proper channels, accepting personal cost.

Nitin: that's so wrong. I'm furious
Chinmay: me too. I wanted to confront the admin head in the staff room today
Nitin: don't. he'll just deny it and you'll look like the troublemaker
Chinmay: so what then? let it go?
Nitin: no. make copies of both sets. I'll check my batches too
Nitin: Priya ma'am said she noticed something last term
Chinmay: ok. if three of us sign, we send it to the university grievance cell
Nitin: my contract renewal is in March
Chinmay: mine too. I know what it might cost
Nitin: …I'm in. copying my sheets tonight
Chinmay: thank you. these kids did the work

qa.q: How many students' marks were changed?
How is Chinmay feeling about what the office did?
qa.a: Chinmay is furious and outraged that students' marks were lowered because of fees.

qa.q: What approach did Chinmay and Nitin choose, and why is it wise?
qa.a: They gathered evidence, found allies like Priya ma'am, and planned to go to the university grievance cell rather than confronting the admin head alone.

qa.q: What is Nitin worried about when he mentions his contract renewal?
qa.a: Nitin is anxious that speaking up could cost Nitin the job, but decides to join anyway.

grounding: Shows young lecturers channelling moral outrage into evidence, allies and a proper channel while accepting the personal cost.
